title: Master Cartography and Rhino Handoff
summary: Create a reviewable three-map planning presentation and coordinate site-design work with the child Rhino instance through McNeel's MCP peer.
preconditions: An ArcGIS Pro project is open and licensed.
Each source path or service URL is readable by the ArcGIS Pro process.
The caller has obtained the current workspace revision.
Rhino.Inside and McNeel's Rhino MCP platform are running before the handoff step when Rhino editing is required.
visualChecks: All three maps are represented in the multi-map layout.
The basemap remains subordinate to thematic layers.
Zoning and transit labels remain legible at the target layout scale.
The proposed site design is distinguishable from existing-building context.
The final layout capture has balanced margins and no blank map frames.
recoveryGuidance: Clear feature selections before exporting presentation images.
Use GlobalID-enabled feature classes for durable identity; do not raw-pull repeatedly into an already-linked Rhino layer. Preview and locally approve sync instead.
After saving GIS edits and reopening documents, inspect sync preview before applying changes. Never auto-resolve unexpected deletions or duplicate identities.

After a workspace_revision_mismatch rejection, refresh state and revalidate before issuing a new request. After outcome_unknown, inspect the workspace and replay only the exact original idempotency key, arguments, immutable workflow version and original revision; do not blindly rerun with a fresh revision.

Request risky-operation review through approval_request, poll approval_status, then invoke unchanged arguments and revision with the single-use token. Only a person in the ArcGIS panel can approve; no remote approval is available.
Use layer.list to resolve an ambiguous or renamed layer before replaying cartography steps.
Start Rhino.Inside and verify rhino.peer-state before retrying a handoff.
Inspect the final PNG and adjust individual registry operations before saving a new workflow version.
